history.period: Believed to be around 400 years old (per local travel guides - weakly sourced, verify)
history.summary: The Shivala Sangliwala Temple is a Shiva temple in the Old Ludhiana area, described in local travel guides as one of the city's prominent Hindu shrines and believed to be about 400 years old (verify - no authoritative history found). It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is best known for its Shivratri crowds: every year during Maha Shivaratri, pilgrims from distant areas visit to offer holy water of the River Ganges to the idols/Shivalingams, and some undertake the arduous Kanwar journey from Haridwar to Ludhiana for the purpose. One place listing ('Prachin Temple Sanglan Shivala', Wool Market Rd near Aggarwal Dharamshala, hours 5:30 AM-9:30 PM) may refer to this same shrine - verify before merging. Ludhiana has many small shivalas; this one is the old-city temple featured in city pilgrimage lists.

name: Shivala Sangliwala Temple
town_description: Ludhiana is Punjab's largest industrial city, set on the Grand Trunk Road along the old course of the Sutlej. The old city quarters around Field Ganj, Chaura Bazar and the wool market hold the town's historic shrines, including this Shiva temple.

travel.airport: Sahnewal Airport (Ludhiana) has limited service (verify); nearest major airport is Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~135 km) or Chandigarh (~100 km).
travel.railway: Ludhiana Junction on the Delhi-Amritsar line; autos/cycle rickshaws to the old city.
travel.road: On NH-44 (Grand Trunk Road); the old city is central Ludhiana, reached by local buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for weather; Maha Shivaratri (Feb-Mar) for the festival, though extremely crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: A listing for a similarly named shrine gives 5:30 AM-9:30 PM daily (verify whether it is this temple). Shivratri draws long queues; visit early in the morning.
